admissible_source_evidence.variant_a: A gentle reminder from the hall keeper, offered with thanks in advance for everyone's patience. Quiet hours in the reading room run, as they long have, from the evening bell until breakfast; the house meeting set these hours and nothing about them has changed, so please treat this as a reminder only and never as a new rule. The reason for the custom is perhaps worth restating: the reading room is the one room where anyone can count on silence for a letter, a ledger, or a difficult chapter, and the custom only holds if it holds every evening, not merely most evenings - so conversation is kindly kept out of the reading room between the bell and breakfast. Anyone who would rather talk after the bell will find the morning room open at any hour, and very pleasant it is too. If the hours ever seem wrong for the season, that would kindly be raised with the house meeting rather than with this notice. The hall keeper is glad to answer any question about it, and thanks you again for keeping the room what it is.
admissible_source_evidence.variant_b: Reminder from the hall keeper. Quiet hours in the reading room run from the evening bell to breakfast. The house meeting set these hours and they have not changed; this is a reminder only, not a new rule. Keep conversation out of the reading room between the bell and breakfast. The morning room is open for talk at any hour. If the hours ever seem wrong for the season, that is a matter for the house meeting, not for this notice. Questions go to the hall keeper.
